ko.executive_summary: MediaTek Q3 revenue reached NT$168 billion, beating guidance, with data center business expected to drive growth in 2026. Samsung System LSI retreating from automotive APs to prioritize higher-margin chips, while Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra is reportedly switching globally to Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 over Exynos. India's semiconductor push and agentic AI are reshaping telecom and connected devices.
key_facts: Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 unveiled at IMC 2026
Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra reportedly using Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 worldwide
Department of War committed $1.5 billion loan to Wolfspeed for national security applications
Samsung System LSI retreating from automotive AP market

implications.text: Qualcomm strengthening mobile SoC market dominance as Samsung exits automotive APs and MediaTek refocuses on data center segment
US government loan commitment to Wolfspeed emphasizes semiconductor supply chain security and reduced China dependence
Samsung's retreat from lower-margin automotive chips signals industry shift toward higher-value AI and data center segments

ko.counterpoint: MediaTek's data center growth ambitions may face intense competition from established players like Nvidia and AMD.
